clue.text: Dreadnought made of this Himalayan cedar ?

indicators.note: something made of materials is built by reshaping them, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: split as dread plus nought, and nought is the letter O

explanation.surface: A battleship built from the timber of an Indian tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadnought' looks like the famous battleship, but split it into DREAD and NOUGHT (O); 'made of' says rearrange DREAD + O into the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a large evergreen conifer native to the western Himalayas.

clue.text: Make out: two notes and nothing more

parts.note: D and E, two notes of the musical scale
a cipher is a zero, or a person who is nothing more than a nonentity

explanation.surface: Interpret a message: just a couple of notes, that's all.
explanation.definitionFit: To read or work out the sense of something obscure, such as a code or bad handwriting.

clue.text: One was in Linden Lea, or -a West country town

parts.note: taken as written
Chard is a market town in Somerset, in the West Country of England

explanation.surface: A song-title place, or perhaps a town in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linden Lea' is the William Barnes poem set by Vaughan Williams, where apple trees bow in the orchard. The West Country is south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's speaker longs for the apple trees of a fruit garden in Linden Lea.

clue.text: The dressing, of certain pretty maids

definitions.meaning: in drill, dressing the ranks means lining soldiers up straight
the nursery rhyme Mary, Mary has pretty maids all in a row

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dressing ranks get into a straight line, as the rhyme's pretty maids stand in a row.

clue.text: Women's movement has fish-eater brought back to book

parts.note: women's lib, short for women's liberation

indicators.note: brought back means the animal's name is turned round, read from the end

parts.note: the otter is a river animal that lives on fish

explanation.surface: Feminists take in a returning otter and turn it into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns OTTER into RETTO, which follows LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: The book of an opera or musical is its text, the words set to music.

clue.text: Like Wordsworth's child vis-a vis man, or vice versa Bultitude Junior

definitions.text: Like Wordsworth's child vis-a vis man, or vice versa Bultitude Junior

parts.words: Like Wordsworth's child vis-a vis man, or vice versa Bultitude Junior
parts.note: Wordsworth wrote that the child is father of the man; in Anstey's novel Vice Versa the boy Dick Bultitude swaps bodies with his father, so each stands in the other's role

explanation.walkthrough: 'vice versa' names F. Anstey's 1882 novel as well as meaning the other way round; in it father and son exchange bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means acting in the role of a parent, as the child-father and the swapped son do.

clue.text: Classic French story

definitions.meaning: of ancient Rome, as in classical antiquity
the French word for a novel

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Rome is the classical world, and a French novel is called by this same word.

clue.text: Ongar and Edgware are not found on the Circle Line

definitions.text: Ongar and Edgware are not found on the Circle Line

parts.words: Ongar and Edgware are not found on the Circle Line
parts.note: Ongar and Edgware were end stations of London Underground lines; a line running in a loop has no end stations

explanation.walkthrough: Ongar (then on the Central line) and Edgware (Northern line) were end-of-line stations; the Circle line, a closed loop, has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends of the line are the stations where trains turn back, which a loop line lacks.

clue.text: Loves protracted tea

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so two loves give two Os
long means drawn out in time

explanation.surface: Long-drawn-out affection over a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark Chinese variety of partly fermented tea leaf.

clue.text: Red ring, Germany, madly fiddling the elections

indicators.note: madly says the letters of the three words are thrown into a wild new order

explanation.surface: A communist network in Germany wildly rigging the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges RED, RING and GERMANY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Redrawing constituency boundaries to favour one party is a way of rigging electoral results.

clue.text: Insect makes cook see red

definitions.meaning: a scale insect of Mexico, dried to give a dye
the red food colouring a cook adds to icing and sauces

explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers the bug and the crimson dye made from its crushed bodies, used to colour food.

clue.text: A lesson in everything, the Duchess told Alice

definitions.meaning: the teaching a fable or story ends with

definitions.text: in everything, the Duchess told Alice
definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Duchess says everything's got one, if only you can find it

explanation.definitionFit: A fable's closing lesson is what the Duchess insists every thing contains, in Lewis Carroll's book.

clue.text: One wooed by a builder in a permissive society

definitions.text: One wooed by a builder in a permissive society

parts.words: One wooed by a builder in a permissive society
parts.note: a builder needs permission to build, so courts the council official who grants it; 'permissive society' is the sixties catchphrase used for the society that grants permits

explanation.walkthrough: 'permissive society' suggests the swinging sixties and romance, but here it is a society where building needs a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: Local-authority officials decide planning applications, so builders court their favour.

clue.text: Send the Poles into a vantage-point

indicators.note: into means the poles' letters go inside the word for a vantage-point

parts.note: a coign, as in Shakespeare's 'coign of vantage', a projecting corner giving a good view
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Dispatch the Polish people up to a lookout tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to dispatch them to someone.

clue.text: Furnish quarters right

parts.note: E and N, east and north, two compass quarters
what is due to someone is theirs by right

explanation.surface: A request to fit out the living quarters properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to supply or endow them with it.

clue.text: Chip time-perhaps some find the odour so ?

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of the two words might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: At fish-and-chip time some people find the smell offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephitic means foul-smelling or noxious, like the stench of a sulphurous vapour.

clue.text: Peruvian navy took food in a body

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of Peru
RN, the Royal Navy
ate, the past of eat

explanation.surface: Peru's navy had a meal on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarnate describes a spirit given flesh, embodied in human form.

clue.text: On one's beam-ends when taken to the cleaners ?

definitions.text: On one's beam-ends when taken to the cleaners ?

parts.words: On one's beam-ends when taken to the cleaners ?
parts.note: a wooden ship was laid over on its side to have its hull scraped clean; on one's beam-ends also means broke, as after being taken to the cleaners

explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to the cleaners' and 'on one's beam-ends' both suggest losing all one's money, but the picture is a ship tipped over for hull cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships were turned on their sides for scraping and repair of the hull.

clue.text: Speed reducer ?

parts.note: read speed as the verb, to hurry, and the thing that does it reduces the time taken, not the speed

explanation.walkthrough: A 'speed reducer' sounds like a brake; it is one that hurries things along and so cuts the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that speeds a process up shortens it, reducing the wait.

clue.text: In a former railway a doctor or hospital worker

indicators.note: In places the doctor inside the letters for the old railway

parts.note: the LNER, London and North Eastern Railway, before British nationalisation
MO, medical officer

explanation.surface: In the days of an old railway, a doctor or a hospital worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The LNER was one of Britain's big four railway companies before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals this was a social worker dealing with patients' welfare.

clue.text: A drink for the Titipu headsman, say

indicators.note: say signals the name is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Ko-Ko, the Lord High Executioner of Titipu in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado

explanation.surface: Offering a beverage to the executioner in The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate-flavoured beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: One having the honour to take a girl a goblet

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour, a British order
Alice, a girl's name

explanation.surface: An honoured guest takes a young woman a wine cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large cup, especially the one used for wine at Communion.

clue.text: Topping for a judge with stomach upset chez Hiawatha

parts.note: a judge's wig, worn on top of the head

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a maw is an animal's stomach or throat

explanation.surface: A judge with an upset stomach visits the home of Longfellow's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chez' is French for 'at the home of'; Hiawatha is the hero of Longfellow's poem, who lived in such a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's Native American hero lives in a domed dwelling of bark or skins.

clue.text: Duck is among the dimmer sea-birds

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A duck is one of the dimmer birds of the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across dimMER SEa, starting inside 'dimmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water.

clue.text: They have a central meeting point

definitions.text: They have a central meeting point

parts.words: They have a central meeting point
parts.note: lines from a circle's centre to its edge all meet at the middle

explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting point' suggests a place for a rendezvous; it is the centre of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Every line from the centre to the rim of a circle starts at the same point.

clue.text: Oriental seaman ran back to tell the tale

indicators.note: back means the whole run of pieces is turned and read from the end

parts.note: E, for east
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: An eastern sailor ran home to recount his adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns E + TAR + RAN as one string: ETARRAN read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell it in order.

clue.text: Pale boy wasted away

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly
Ed, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pallid lad who has grown thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon diminishes in its phases; so does anything that declines or fades.

clue.text: Flattery that may be sincere, if not genuine

definitions.meaning: from the saying that copying is the sincerest form of flattery
a fake or copy, not the real thing

explanation.definitionFit: Copying is called the sincerest flattery, and a copy is also a fake.

clue.text: Its tables bore Elsinore's funeral baked-meats

definitions.text: Its tables bore Elsinore's funeral baked-meats

parts.words: Its tables bore Elsinore's funeral baked-meats
parts.note: Hamlet complains the funeral baked meats did coldly furnish forth the tables of his mother's wedding, so soon after his father's death

explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore is the castle in Hamlet; the leftovers from the funeral were served at Gertrude's wedding to Claudius.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude's wedding feast followed her husband's funeral so quickly the food was reused.

clue.text: Saw, but not that which might by a carpenter

parts.words: but not that which might by a carpenter
parts.note: fill the blank: a carpenter's saw is a tool which might ..., so split the word as two

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the carpenter's tool, but it is the past tense of see; split the answer into BE HELD to fill the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of see is the same as having looked at or observed.
